### `Pass 258.0` (`5c2b61f` + `d39aa33`, 2026-09-06) — ★★★★ **THE BORDER LINE STYLE: A DASHED MARK IN THE OPERATOR'S FILE WAS SILENTLY SOLIDIFIED THE FIRST TIME ITS COLOUR WAS CHANGED — DISCLOSED, WHICH IS THE FLOOR AND NOT THE CEILING — AND FOUR APPEARANCE-REGENERATION ROUTES CARRIED THE DEFECT, NOT THE ONE REPORTED** — ★★★ **`MarkupStyle::endings` COULD BE SET BUT NEVER REMOVED: THE NEAREST A CALLER COULD GET WAS `[/None /None]`, WHICH IS TABLE 176'S OWN DEFAULT AND THEREFORE THE LEAST INFORMATIVE KEY AVAILABLE** — ★★ **A `width` ON A TEXT MARKUP RETURNED `Ok` WITH AN EMPTY `dropped` AND DID NOTHING; NOW `EditError::StylePropertyNotApplicable`, PLUS A `MarkupStyleSupport` PREDICATE SO A SHELL CAN ASK INSTEAD OF CARRYING ITS OWN COPY OF THE LIST** — ★ **BREAKING: `MarkupStyle` LOSES `Copy`; `endings` CHANGES TYPE** — three `pdfcer-gui` requests of 2026-09-06 in one seam, minted and shipped in one filing

**The defect, in the requester's words, and it is a loss of the operator's
own work rather than a missing feature:**

> *"A dashed mark that already exists in the operator's file is silently
> converted to a solid one the first time he changes its colour."*

**The mechanism, and nothing in it was wrong on its own.**
`set_markup_style` regenerates `/AP` from `annot_author::spec_from_dict`; the
spec had no dash field; the rebuilt appearance was therefore solid. `/BS /D`
**survived in the dictionary**, and under **`R43`** pdfcer paints from `/AP`
— so the file's two halves disagreed and the appearance won.

**It was disclosed** (`DroppedProperty::DashPattern` fired), and the
requester put the distinction better than a rule could:

> *"An operator who wanted a red dashed cloud and pressed the colour swatch
> has been given a red solid one, and 'we told you' is a poor second to 'we
> kept it'."*

**The fix follows `Pass 98.0`'s `/BE` precedent exactly** — read the property
back on the way **in**, so a regeneration re-authors it — rather than growing
`MarkupStyle` a field and calling the loss disclosed. All three asks landed,
not only the preservation the requester said they would take alone, because
once the dash was in the pipeline the other two were nearly free: **preserve**
(`/BS` `/S` + `/D` read back; a restyle that does not mention `dash` keeps
one, **including a dash pdfcer never authored**), **author**
(`MarkupOptions::dash`, CLI `add-markup --dash 4,2`), **restyle**
(`MarkupStyle::dash: Option<StyleEdit<BorderDash>>` — `Set` dashes, `Clear`
solidifies, `None` leaves alone).

**★★ FOUR ROUTES REGENERATE AN APPEARANCE, AND THE REPORT NAMED ONE.**
`set_markup_style` is the reported route. `resize_annotation`,
`reshape_annotation` and `add_markup_inner` bake through the same generator
and **would all have solidified a dash too** — so the defect was reachable by
dragging a resize handle or a vertex, not only by pressing a swatch. All four
carry the dash now, **each proven by a separate sabotage**. This is `R219`'s
obligation discharged at authoring time rather than discovered by the shell
one route at a time.

**The shape of `dash` in the API — `AppearanceOptions`, not a `MarkupSpec`
field, and the precedent is named rather than invented.** A dash cuts across
the stroked subtypes exactly as `QuadPointOrder` cuts across the text-markup
ones, and that is the **house precedent this follows** — it does not set one,
which is why no decision record is minted for it. Cost: **~15 call sites
instead of ~190** (a field on seven `MarkupSpec` variants). New public items:
`annot_author::BorderDash`, `annot_author::AppearanceOptions`,
`annot_author::build_appearance_opts`.

**Two spec facts the model refuses to invent, both sourced before coding:**

- **`BorderDash` carries NO PHASE.** Table 166's `/D` is the array alone, and
  the standard says the phase *"shall be assumed 0"* — so modelling a phase
  would invent a value **the file cannot express**. The channel reply tells
  the shell not to offer a phase control, for the same reason.
- **`BorderDash::new` enforces §8.4.3.6 at construction** (every element
  non-negative, not all zero; the empty array *is* the solid line) and returns
  `Option`. **Table 166's `/D` default `[3]` is honoured** for a `/BS /S /D`
  carrying no array — read as `[3]`, not as solid.

**The second request — `endings` could be SET but never REMOVED.**
`MarkupStyle::endings` was a bare `Option<(LineEnding, LineEnding)>` while its
three siblings were `Option<StyleEdit<_>>`. The nearest a caller could get to
removing `/LE` was writing `[/None /None]` — and **Table 176's default for
both ends is `/None`**, making that the least informative key available: it
says exactly what its own absence would have said. **A file could not be
returned to the state it was opened in, in a key neither UI shows.** The
requester's deciding argument was a signed drawing and *"is this
byte-identical to what my client sent me"*; it beat the cheaper doc-comment
alternative they themselves offered. `Clear` now removes `/LE`; `Set` writes
it, `Set((None, None))` included if a caller ever wants the key present and
empty-handed.

**The third request — a `width` on a text markup was silently swallowed.**
`Ok`, no error, no `DroppedProperty`, nothing changed:
`MarkupSpec::TextMarkup` has no border to widen. **A shell trusting that pair
was entitled to tell the operator the width took.** Now refused by name —
`EditError::StylePropertyNotApplicable { id, subtype, property }`, one
showable sentence, **refused before anything is written so the session is
untouched**. And the shell gets to ask in advance:
`edit::MarkupStyleSupport::for_subtype(&[u8])` → `takes_border`,
`takes_interior`, `takes_endings`. The requester's own sentence is quoted into
its doc comment because it is the justification:

> *"That list is the engine's to know. The first subtype that gains or loses a
> border is the day our copy is wrong and nothing tells us."*

**The alternative they offered and we declined, with their own reasoning:**
reporting the ignored width as a `DroppedProperty` instead of refusing. A
`dropped` entry means **the file lost something**; here nothing was lost — the
**request** was ignored. Different sentences to an operator, and `dropped`
keeps its meaning. `R221`'s hazard is closed too: **a test asserts the
predicate and the refusal agree**, so a drift between them fails pdfcer's
build rather than the shell's.

**BREAKING, both predicted by the requester:**
1. **`MarkupStyle` is no longer `Copy`** (`BorderDash` owns a `Vec<f64>`); it
   stays `Clone + Default + PartialEq`. Implicit copies become move errors,
   all mechanical.
2. **`MarkupStyle::endings` changes type** to `Option<StyleEdit<(LineEnding,
   LineEnding)>>`.

**Tests — `crates/pdfcer-core/tests/markup_border_style.rs` (627 lines, 15
tests), each verified non-vacuous by sabotage (relayed):**
`a_colour_change_does_not_solidify_a_dashed_border`,
`a_resize_does_not_solidify_a_dashed_border`,
`a_reshape_does_not_solidify_a_dashed_border` (the three regeneration routes
the report did not name, plus `authoring_solid_is_unchanged_by_this_pass` for
the fourth), `clearing_the_dash_makes_it_solid_in_dictionary_and_appearance`,
`a_solid_mark_can_be_made_dashed`,
`an_unusable_dash_pattern_is_refused_at_construction`,
`clearing_the_endings_removes_the_key`,
`setting_none_none_still_writes_the_key` (the two states Table 176 makes
distinguishable), `a_width_on_a_text_markup_is_refused_by_name`,
`a_dash_on_a_text_markup_is_refused_by_name`,
`endings_on_a_square_are_refused_by_name`,
`a_refused_property_leaves_the_session_untouched`,
`the_support_matrix_answers_in_advance`, `the_predicate_and_the_refusal_agree`.

**Acceptance criteria — written at ship, from the three requests, all met:**
1. A restyle that does not mention `dash` preserves an existing one, including
   a foreign dash — **met** (test 1; the other three routes tests 2–4).
2. A dash can be authored and cleared through both shells — **met**
   (`MarkupOptions::dash`, `MarkupStyle::dash`, CLI `add-markup --dash` and
   `set-markup-style --dash ON,OFF,…|solid`).
3. `/LE` can be removed, not only set to its own default — **met**.
4. A property the subtype cannot take is refused by name with nothing written,
   and a predicate answers in advance — **met**; the `DroppedProperty`
   alternative **declined** with the requester's own reasoning.
5. `DroppedProperty::BorderStyle`/`::DashPattern` stop firing on a preserved
   dash, and the in-crate disclosure test is **updated in place with the
   reasoning** rather than deleted — **met** (`edit.rs:44983–45002`; the same
   file already documented `Pass 98.0`'s identical narrowing of
   `BorderEffect`).

**Not in this Pass:** `/S /B`, `/S /I` and `/S /U` (beveled, inset,
underline) are still authored as solid and still disclosed — a dash is the
one non-solid style with a §8.4.3.6 model behind it. **Owed (reported, not
edited — this role does not touch `crates/`):** four of the six rule-11
survivors above are this Pass's — `edit.rs:4887`, `edit.rs:4890`,
`main.rs:30924`, `main.rs:30928`.

### `Pass 258.1` (`5c2b61f`, 2026-09-06) — ★★★★ **A `/FreeText`'s PAINTED WORDS NOW FOLLOW ITS NOTE: `set_markup_note` CHANGED `/Contents` AND LEFT THE PAGE PAINTING THE OLD TEXT — THE ONLY PLACE AN OPERATOR COULD TYPE WORDS, PRESS SAVE, SEE NO ERROR, AND HAVE THE DOCUMENT NOT SAY WHAT THEY WROTE** — ★★★ **`annot_author::text_spec_from_dict` — THE READER `pdfcer-gui` IDENTIFIED AS THE SINGLE BLOCKER UNDER THREE SURFACES — NOW EXISTS AND IS PUBLIC** — ★★ **`multiline` IS NOT IN THE FILE (§12.5.6.6 GIVES THE SUBTYPE NO SUCH KEY), SO IT IS *MEASURED*: BAKE THE ORIGINAL TEXT BOTH WAYS AND COMPARE AGAINST THE BYTES ON DISK — ONE COMPARISON ANSWERING TWO QUESTIONS** — ★ **A FOREIGN APPEARANCE IS LEFT ALONE AND REPORTED, NEVER REPLACED WITH pdfcer's PLAINER RENDERING** — minted and shipped in one filing

**Why the two values diverge with no visible first moment.**
`annot_author::free_text` bakes `/AP` `/N` from the caller's text **and then
writes the same string into `/Contents`**, so the two agree **exactly** when
the box is placed. `write_markup_note`'s command carried the annotation
object only, never the appearance stream. `R43` means pdfcer paints from
`/AP`. Every one of those three was correct in isolation; together they made
the note verb's own documentation — *"a note is content the operator cannot
recover from the canvas"* — **backwards for this one subtype**, where
`/Contents` **is** the appearance's input.

**★ It is `/FreeText` ONLY, and the family is deliberately not uniform:**

| `/Subtype` | is `/Contents` painted? | `set_markup_note` before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/FreeText` | **yes** — it is the appearance's own input | stale | **re-baked** |
| `/Text` (sticky) | no — shown by the reader's popup | correct | **unchanged** |
| `/Stamp` | no — a comment *about* the stamp; never written by `stamp()` | correct | **unchanged** |

**The stamp row is the opposite of a defect and the requester said so by
name:** *"Please do not 'fix' it by making a stamp's note drive its label —
that would break the one of the three that is currently right."* That
paragraph is **quoted into the test that pins it**, so it is asserted rather
than merely intended.

**The re-bake is inside `set_markup_note`, not a second verb.** The requester
asked for exactly that — *"rather than a second verb you might forget to
call"* — and it ships as **one call, one undo entry, both halves**.

**★★ `multiline` is MEASURED, because the file does not carry it.**
§12.5.6.6 gives `/FreeText` no multiline flag — `/Ff` is a **form-field** key
and a `/FreeText` is not a field. So the re-bake bakes the **original** text
**both ways** and compares each against the appearance already on disk. A
match names the layout **and** proves the appearance is pdfcer's own; no match
means it is foreign and must be left alone. **One measurement, both answers**
— the same trick `set_markup_style` uses, with one more degree of freedom.
Consequence a shell must know: **`TextAnnotSpec::FreeText::multiline` coming
back from `text_spec_from_dict` is ALWAYS `false` and must not be believed**;
a caller re-authoring a `/FreeText` itself has to run the same comparison or
supply the value.

**The blocker under three surfaces, now removed.**
`annot_author::text_spec_from_dict` reads `/FreeText`, `/Text` and `/Stamp`
back into `TextAnnotSpec`. Without it there was no way to re-author a placed
`/FreeText`, **and** no way to change a sticky note's icon and colour
(`request_a_sticky_notes_icon_and_colour_cannot_be_changed.md`, still open),
**and** no way to serve the clipboard's `FreeText | Text | Stamp` arm. One
reader, three surfaces.

**New disclosure field: `MarkupNoteChange::appearance_rebaked: bool.**
`true` when the picture moved with the words. **`false` is not a failure** —
it is correct and final on a sticky, on a stamp, and on a `/FreeText` whose
appearance pdfcer did not author. A status line can finally say **which half
moved**. Rule 4 shape: the re-bake **renders exactly as saved content will
render** (no badge, no provisional marking on the page) and the disclosure
that pdfcer inferred the layout lives **off-canvas**, in the returned report
and the CLI's printed line.

**The authoring-time trap, closed before it cost anyone anything.** Passing
both `TextAnnotSpec::FreeText { text }` and `MarkupOptions::note` with
**different** words produced a document whose two halves disagreed **from
creation**. The requester called it *"a loaded gun on a verb whose two
arguments look independent and are not"*. Now
`EditError::FreeTextNoteConflictsWithText { spec_text, note_text }`.
**Identical strings are still allowed** — that is what the authoring path
writes anyway, so refusing them would be refusal on principle.

**Tests — `crates/pdfcer-core/tests/free_text_note_rebake.rs` (588 lines, 11
tests):** `editing_a_free_texts_note_repaints_the_box`,
`the_note_and_the_repaint_are_one_undo_entry`,
`a_multiline_box_stays_multiline_through_an_edit` (the measurement, exercised),
`a_sticky_notes_appearance_is_not_rebaked`,
`a_stamps_note_does_not_become_its_label` (the requester's paragraph, pinned),
`a_foreign_appearance_is_left_alone_and_disclosed`,
`authoring_a_free_text_with_a_conflicting_note_is_refused`,
`authoring_a_free_text_with_a_matching_note_is_allowed`,
`a_free_text_reads_back`,
`a_sticky_note_reads_back_including_its_icon_and_colour`,
`a_non_text_subtype_is_refused_by_name`. Assertions are made **against the
saved bytes** (`painted_text` re-parses an incremental save), not against the
session overlay — `R159`, and the right choice here because the whole defect
was a file whose dictionary and appearance disagreed.

**★★ THE `R162` INSTANCE, AND IT IS THE REASON THE FILE IS WORTH READING.**
The first version of `a_foreign_appearance_is_left_alone_and_disclosed`
asserted `!change.appearance_rebaked` — **and passed with the entire re-bake
disabled.** A `"not X"` assertion is vacuous when the feature that would
produce `X` is absent, which is `R162` exactly, with the container being a
single `bool` rather than a collection. It became a test only once a
**control** asserting the positive sat beside it (`control_change
.appearance_rebaked` must be `true` on an unmodified pdfcer appearance),
carrying the reasoning in a comment the next reader will meet:

> *"'Not re-baked' is equally true of a re-bake that is DISABLED, so this
> assertion measured nothing until the same edit was shown to re-bake when
> the appearance is left alone."*

**A second sabotage found a different thing, and the engineer recorded the
distinction rather than the reassurance.** Widening the `/FreeText` subtype
guard (`edit.rs:26247`) to apply to **every** subtype left the sticky-note and
stamp tests **GREEN**. The real protection is **structural and one level
down** — `rebake_free_text_appearance` destructures the `TextAnnotSpec` as
`FreeText` and returns `None` for anything else, whatever the guard says. That
is written into the code as a comment (*"this subtype test is a FAST PATH, not
the guarantee … worth knowing rather than mistaking for those tests guarding
it"*) instead of leaving two tests looking like they guard something they do
not. This half is **`R221`'s** cause — two agreeing implementations of one
predicate, mutually masking — correctly diagnosed and correctly left in place,
since the redundant one is a cheap fast path and the doc comment now says so.

**Acceptance criteria — written at ship, all met:**
1. A `/FreeText`'s note edit repaints the box, in one command and one undo
   entry — **met**.
2. Sticky and stamp are untouched, asserted not assumed — **met**.
3. A foreign appearance survives intact, the note still commits, and
   `appearance_rebaked` is `false` — **met**, with the positive control beside
   it.
4. `multiline` is recovered without inventing a key the spec has not — **met**
   (measured; the reader's own field is documented as unusable).
5. The authoring-time conflict is refused by name — **met**; identical strings
   allowed.

**Owed (reported, not edited):** rule-11 survivors 5 and 6 — `edit.rs:15614`
and `edit.rs:26099`, the *"a note is content the operator cannot recover from
the canvas"* sentence, now backwards for the one subtype this Pass changed,
in two spellings.

### `Pass 258.2` (`5c2b61f`, 2026-09-06) — ★★★ **WHICH FILE DOES THIS BOOKMARK OPEN? `/Launch` ACTIONS NOW REPORT THE FILE THEY NAME — THE RESOLVER ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS SIMPLY NOT CALLED FOR `/Launch`, SO EVERYTHING BUT THE ACTION'S `/S` WAS DISCARDED** — ★★ **`list-outline` STOPS PRINTING DESTINATIONS WITH RUST'S `{:?}`: A `/GoToR` FILENAME WAS REACHING OPERATORS AS A DECIMAL BYTE ARRAY WHILE `list-links` HAD THE READABLE RENDERER ALL ALONG** — ★ **READING IS NOT RUNNING: `R13` IS UNTOUCHED — THIS IS A FILENAME TO SHOW** — an operator ask, minted and shipped in one filing

**The ask, and why two other tools could not answer it.** A folder of PDFs,
one a table of contents whose bookmarks open the others; the operator wanted
*"the name of the bookmark and the filename it points to"*. `cpdf` gave
`<</F 251 0 R/S/Launch>>` — an **unresolved indirect reference** to a file
specification. `pdftk` gave `BookmarkPageNumber: 0`, which is `pdftk`
correctly reporting that the bookmark names no page **in this document** while
saying nothing about the file it does name.

**pdfcer's own gap was narrower and slightly worse.** `file_spec_bytes` — the
resolver that turns `251 0 R` into `chapter1.pdf` — **already existed and was
already used for `/GoToR`**. `read_action` simply did not call it for
`/Launch`, so `Destination::NonNavigation` could say *"this bookmark launches
something"* and never **what**. `Destination::NonNavigation` gains a
`file: Option<Vec<u8>>` field. `/Launch` stays a non-navigation action — it
starts an application, it is not a jump — but *"which file"* is answerable,
and **refusing to answer it was an omission rather than a position**.

**Where the filename is read from, and why three spellings.** Table 203 (ISO
32000-2 Table 207) makes `/Launch`'s `/F` **required unless** `/Win`, `/Mac`
or `/Unix` is present, and those three are **deprecated in PDF 2.0**
(§12.6.4.6: *"The `F` entry determines the file specification platform to be
launched"*). So `/F` is tried first and the `/Win` sub-dictionary's own bare
`/F` second. `None` for every other action type, for a `/Launch` with no
usable entry (Table 203's own *"it shall do nothing"* case), and for a file
specification in a shape the module does not read.

**The second half, which nobody asked for and which was worse.** For the
`/GoToR` case where the filename **was** parsed, `list-outline` printed the
destination with Rust's `{:?}` — so the answer reached the operator as
`file: Some([99, 104, 97, …])`. **The information was right and unreadable**,
and `list-links` had had the readable renderer for the same enum the whole
time. `list-outline` now uses it, and gains **`--json`** for a folder-sized
job.

**New fixture — `fixtures/synthetic/outline/toc-launch-targets.pdf` (1,798
B), four bookmarks covering every shape a real table of contents mixes:**

| bookmark | action | file named by |
|---|---|---|
| Chapter 1 | `/Launch` | **indirect** `/F` filespec dict — the operator's exact shape |
| Chapter 2 | `/Launch` | direct `/F` string |
| Appendix | `/Launch` | `/Win << /F >>` only (the 2.0-deprecated fallback) |
| Chapter 3 | `/GoToR` | `/F` + `/D` page |

**★ Reading is not running.** `R13` is untouched. A `/Launch` target is a
filename to **show**, and pdfcer resolves it **precisely so an operator can
see what a document would do without a viewer doing it**. The field's own doc
comment says so at the point of definition, not only in this entry.

**Tests — `crates/pdfcer-core/tests/outline_launch_targets.rs` (196 lines, 5
tests):** `every_bookmark_reports_the_file_it_opens` (★ the ask itself: title
→ filename for all four), `an_indirect_file_specification_resolves`,
`a_win_platform_dictionary_is_read_when_f_is_absent`,
`a_launch_is_still_not_a_page_destination` (the boundary — resolving a
filename did not turn `/Launch` into navigation),
`an_action_without_a_file_reports_none`.

**Acceptance criteria — written at ship, all met:** every bookmark that opens
a file reports it, across all four carrier shapes (**met**); the deprecated
platform fallback is read and is not preferred (**met**); `/Launch` does not
become a page destination (**met**); the CLI prints it readably and offers
`--json` (**met**); `R13` unchanged, nothing executed (**met**).

### `Pass 258.3` (`5c2b61f`, 2026-09-06) — ★★★★ **`merge` RE-POINTS CROSS-FILE BOOKMARKS INSTEAD OF DROPPING THEM — MEASURED FIRST: MERGING A TABLE OF CONTENTS WITH THE FOUR FILES ITS BOOKMARKS LAUNCHED GAVE `outline_kept=0 outline_dropped=4`, EVERY ONE OF THE OPERATOR'S OWN TITLES DISCARDED, HONESTLY BUT COMPLETELY** — ★★★ **ORDER IS THE FIX: RE-POINTING MUST PRECEDE PRUNING, BECAUSE A `/Launch` ENTRY HAS NO PAGE IN ITS OWN SOURCE AND THE PRUNER REACHES IT FIRST** — ★★ **A LINK NAMING A FILE *NOT* IN THE MERGE IS STILL DROPPED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE** — ★ **BREAKING: `pageops::merge` TAKES A THIRD ARGUMENT** — minted and shipped in one filing

**The problem was stated by someone else and confirmed by measurement.** The
operator brought another engineer's answer to his own question, whose closing
paragraph was:

> *"Launch and GoToR actions point at external files by name, so once
> everything is one document the targets no longer exist and the bookmarks
> break. If you merge, you need to rewrite each bookmark to an internal
> destination afterwards."*

**That was accurate about pdfcer**, and it was **measured before anything was
built**: `outline_kept=0 outline_dropped=4`. pdfcer *disclosed* the loss —
**the floor, not the ceiling**, the same distinction `Pass 258.0` turned on
for a dashed border, in the same commit.

**Why the merge can do better than the post-processing script that was
advised.** The advice was to rebuild the mapping afterwards. But **the merge
already knows** which file each source came from: it is **holding the list**.
The mapping the operator would otherwise reconstruct by hand is **free at
exactly the moment it is needed**, and **no other stage of the pipeline has
both halves at once**.

**★★ Order is the fix, and getting it backwards produces a correct-looking
implementation that never fires.** Re-pointing must happen **before**
pruning. A `/Launch` entry has **no page in its own source**, so the pruner
discards it before anything can notice that the file it names is sitting in
the same merge.

**Matching, stated precisely because it is an inference.** By **file name**,
**case-insensitively**, **ignoring directories** — a `/Launch` says
`chapter1.pdf`, not `chapter1`, and not `C:\jobs\chapter1.pdf`. This is
**rule 4** territory: pdfcer is inferring that `chapter1.pdf` in a `/Launch`
means the `chapter1.pdf` in this merge, so it is **disclosed** —
`AssembleReport::outline_items_relinked`, counted **separately from `kept`**
because it is a different fact: these entries did not merely survive, **their
destination was rewritten**, and an operator comparing the merged document
with the original is entitled to know which. The CLI prints
`outline_relinked=` in its token line **and** a named stderr line when the
count is non-zero.

**What is deliberately NOT done.** A link naming a file that was **not**
merged stays unresolved and prunes as before. That bookmark is **genuinely
dead** — the file it names is not in the document and not on the way in — and
**inventing a destination for it would be a worse answer than dropping it and
saying so**. Both counts are reported, so the two outcomes are
distinguishable.

**New API.** `AssembleOptions::source_files: Vec<Vec<u8>>` — each source's
name **on disk**, deliberately separate from `source_titles` (what to *call*
each source in the generated heading, usually a stem and freely chosen). **It
has to be the real name or the match fails.** `AssembleReport
::outline_items_relinked: usize`.

**BREAKING: `pageops::merge` takes a third argument** — the sources' file
names. **`&[]` restores the pre-`258.3` behaviour exactly**, and an empty
slice disables re-pointing entirely, which is what every caller had before.

**Tests — `crates/pdfcer-core/tests/merge_relinks_cross_file_bookmarks.rs`
(344 lines, 5 tests):**
`cross_file_bookmarks_are_repointed_instead_of_dropped`,
`a_repointed_bookmark_lands_on_the_right_page` (a `/GoToR`'s `/D` page
survives the re-point, not merely the file),
`a_link_to_a_file_outside_the_merge_is_still_dropped`,
`without_file_names_nothing_is_repointed` (the `&[]` compatibility path),
`matching_ignores_directories_and_case`. The fixture is built inline and
carries the same four action shapes `258.2`'s fixture does.

**Acceptance criteria — written at ship, all met:** a bookmark whose target
file is also a source is re-pointed at that file's pages, `/GoToR`'s page
included (**met**); re-pointing runs before pruning (**met**, and the test
that would catch the reverse is
`cross_file_bookmarks_are_repointed_instead_of_dropped` against the measured
`0/4` baseline); a link outside the merge is still dropped and counted
(**met**); the inference is disclosed and counted separately from `kept`
(**met**); the old behaviour is reachable with `&[]` (**met**).

**Not in this Pass:** matching by **path** rather than by bare name (a merge
of two `chapter1.pdf` from different folders re-points both at whichever
source matched first — named here as the open case, not owed); and
re-pointing a `/GoToR` **named destination** rather than a page number.

### `Pass 14.6` (`b64ddb6`, 2026-09-06) — ★★★ **A TYPE 0 FONT'S `/FontDescriptor` IS READ FROM THE DESCENDANT CIDFONT (§9.7.4.1, Table 117), NOT THE PARENT WHERE IT NEVER IS — every composite run was `embedded=false`, so `edit-text` told the operator a bundled substitute rendered letters that 8,640 bytes of `/FontFile2` actually render, AND the embedded-subset floor `R-INV-1` had NEVER run on a composite run: a `/ToUnicode` broader than the retained glyphs let a CID reach the writer (MEASURED: `A → B` on a page painting only `A`, `C` went through before, refused `TargetAbsent` now); one resolution change fixes both, the floor itself untouched** — minted and shipped from the inbound queue in the same filing

**Before (`Pass 14.1`'s `classify_font`, measured in source at `c192f76`):**
`font_dict.get(b"FontDescriptor")` on whatever dictionary the run's `Tf`
named. For a simple font that IS the holder. For `/Subtype /Type0` the
holder is `/DescendantFonts[0]` (ISO 32000-1 §9.7.4.1; Table 117 lists
`/FontDescriptor` as required on the CIDFont dictionary and Table 121 does
not list it on the Type 0 dictionary at all), so `descriptor` was `None`,
`embedded` false, `flags` 0, `symbolic` false — on no evidence — for every
composite font on earth. `subset` was unaffected (derived from the
`/BaseFont` tag, which the parent does carry), which is why the report could
read `subset=true` beside `glyph_source=Bundled`.

**After.** A `descriptor_holder` is chosen once: the descendant for `Type0`,
the font dictionary itself otherwise; `/FontDescriptor`, `/Flags`, `symbolic`
and `embedded` all read from it. Nothing downstream changed: the floor at
`edit.rs:1915` (`class.embedded && class.subset`) runs for composite runs
because its condition is now true for them, and `carried_codes` already
collected CIDs on those runs.

**Requester's file (relayed, `pdfcer-gui` 2026-09-05):** `AAAAAA+Arimo-Bold`,
`Type0/CIDFontType2`, `Identity-H`, `embedded=FontFile2 bytes=8640` by
`list-fonts`; `edit-text` on the same font said *NON-embedded*. Two of
pdfcer's own surfaces disagreed about one font in one file, and the one the
operator meets while editing was the wrong one.

**Tests — `crates/pdfcer-core/tests/composite_descriptor.rs`, RUN HERE 2/2:**
- `a_composite_run_with_an_embedded_descendant_is_reported_embedded` —
  `cidfonttype2-partially-injective-tounicode.pdf` (an `ABCDEF+` subset with
  `/FontFile2` on the descendant): `glyph_source == Embedded`, `subset` true,
  no disclosure contains `NON-embedded`.
- `the_embedded_subset_floor_now_guards_composite_runs` —
  `cidfonttype2-subset-floor.pdf`: `A → C` succeeds; `A → B` is
  `EditError::Refused` with `trigger == TargetAbsent`, `character ==
  Some('B')`, message containing `R-INV-1` and `code 2`.
- Sabotage (relayed): the parent read restored fails both.

**Acceptance criteria — written at ship, from the request, all met:**
1. `/FontDescriptor` resolved through `/DescendantFonts[0]` for `/Type0` —
   **met** (`edit.rs:3073–3091`).
2. `EditGlyphSource::Embedded` and no NON-embedded disclosure on an embedded
   composite subset — **met** (test 1).
3. The embedded-subset floor fires on a composite run for a CID that is in
   `/ToUnicode` but not painted on the page — **met** (test 2); the
   requester's §5 alternative (scope the floor to simple fonts by name)
   **declined**, with the fixture as the reason.
4. `flags`/`symbolic` from the same descriptor — **met** (same holder); the
   `R-INV-2` composite branch is reachable but does not fire on a name
   `/Encoding` — **not separately tested** (a composite with a stream
   `/Encoding` is the open case, as the request said).
5. No change to `carried_codes`, the writer, or any sibling fixture — **met**
   (`git show --stat`: four files; `git diff --stat HEAD -- fixtures/` empty).

**Not in this Pass:** a document-scoped floor for composite subsets (the
requester's *"a composite subset is document-scoped"* observation is true and
the page-scoped proxy is kept deliberately — the same proxy simple embedded
subsets get); the stream-`/Encoding` composite case for `R-INV-2`.

**What broke, stated first.** CI run `34024691738` on `c7409d3`
(`2026-09-06 09:27:16Z`): nine jobs green, *repository audits (19 checks)*
red — the step *check every Pass-claiming commit is filed* printed **224
`UNFILED`** lines (`gh run view --log-failed | grep -c UNFILED`; the
`commits-filed` step 0), every one of them a filed Pass commit from weeks
earlier, **every hash EIGHT characters** (`79e259a1`, `743830d6`,
`b8fd06d1`). The same gate was clean on the working clone (`git rev-parse
--short HEAD` = `2da1d62`, seven; `count 5330` loose / `in-pack 11328` /
`packs 1`). **Cause:** `check-passes-filed.py` and `check-commits-filed.py`
join `git log --format=%h` against the record's 7-character citations, and
`%h` under `core.abbrev=auto` is the shortest prefix git judges unique for
the repository's CURRENT object count — floor 7, stepping to 8 as the
repository grows, with the threshold computed from the packed count that a
fresh `actions/checkout` clone (one pack) reaches before a long-lived clone
with loose objects does. The push also carried the 450th filing's unrelated
`encoding="utf-8"` edit to the same gate, which made the wrong cause look
obvious. **Fix:** `--abbrev=7` (`check-passes-filed.py:168`,
`check-commits-filed.py:330`, `check-cited-commits-exist.py:223`) and
`--short=7` (`check-passes-filed.py:233`; `package-portable.py`'s
build-folder name, a stable name rather than a join). **Reproduced HERE,
both directions,** with `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.abbrev=9'"`: the
pre-fix script (`git show 2da1d62~1:tools/check-passes-filed.py`) → **224
`UNFILED`**; the committed script → `passes-filed: clean`. **224 = 224** —
the local reproduction yields CI's exact count, which is what isolates the
abbreviation length from everything else in the push. The dispatch's and the
commit message's *"20 UNFILED"* is CORRECTED to 224 by the CI log (per-step
`uniq -c`); the message's *"224 before, clean after"* was already right.

**`R242` considered and NOT minted.** Candidate offered: *"any tool that
compares abbreviated hashes to text pins the abbreviation length"*, with the
2026-08-11 depth-1 clone (`cd86adc`, 108th filing) as the first occurrence of
*"a filing gate lying in CI for an environmental reason"*. The wider shape is
at n = 2 with a different mechanism and a different fix each time (a refusal
guard vs. a pinned parameter); the sentence is at n = 1. The deciding reason
is `R241`'s own disposition (393rd/394th filings): **where the check is
mechanical, the gate is the rule** — and this check is one grep, which ran
here as the filing's sweep: `%h` / `--short` over `tools/`, `.github/`,
`crates/*/build.rs` with `abbrev=7|short=7` excluded → **ZERO unpinned uses
remain**; every other `rev-parse` in `tools/` returns a full hash or a
non-hash; `verify-release.py` and `check-history-not-rewritten.py` compare
full hashes. **One reported, correct, not touched (`crates/`):**
`crates/pdfcer-core/build.rs:132` — `git describe --tags --always --dirty`
without `--abbrev`, so the banner's `-g<hash>` suffix follows the auto
length across machines; cosmetic, nothing joins on it, and at an exact tag
(the release case) `describe` prints the bare tag. The candidate and its
grep are recorded by name in the RAG entry; mint at a third gate or a second
repository.

**RAG entry (tier 4, `D:/dev/rag/rust/`):**
`gits_default_short_hash_length_grows_with_the_object_count_so_a_gate_joining_h_against_pinned_citations_fails_all_at_once_on_a_fresh_clone.md`
+ `index.md` bullet — the gate-methodology angle (the two-instance table,
why a pinned parameter beats a refusal guard where available, the candidate
rule and its grep, the survivors). CROSS-REFERENCES the engineer's

**What a caller sees, stated first.** A form author places an empty
signature field — the "sign here" placeholder every form workflow produces —
and until this commit `pdfcer sign --field-name <that name>` was refused as a
collision (`FieldNameTaken`); pdfcer could only add a SECOND field beside
the author's. Now `SignRequest::field_name` naming an EXISTING field is
resolved BEFORE any object number is allocated
(`EditSession::reusable_sig_field`, `edit.rs:22724`): an empty, merged
`/FT /Sig` field is **signed into** — `/V` ← the signature dictionary, the
field's own `/Rect` and page (`/P`, else the page whose `/Annots` lists it)
place the appearance (a degenerate rect = invisible), every other entry of
the author's dictionary survives, no widget is appended to `/Annots`,
`/Fields` is untouched, `/AcroForm /SigFlags |= 3` through a new
`acroform_sigflags_write` (`edit.rs:22884`). An unknown name still CREATES,
unchanged. The CLI prints `field=<name> (existing|created)`
(`main.rs:27393`), `field_lock: /FieldMDP <All|Include: a, b|Exclude: …>
(copied from the field's /Lock, Table 233)` (`main.rs:27418`) and `note:
seed value: …` lines; the six new refusals exit `9`. **Measured by the
core test, not asserted:** the pre-existing objects re-emitted are EXACTLY
the field and the AcroForm holder (the catalog — the fixture's form is
inline) — asserted as the set `{1, 5}` on `sig-field-empty.pdf`; and
`parse_acroform` sees ONE `/Sig` field afterwards, not two.

engineer's-choice recorded):**

### `Pass 10.13` (`ab40127`, 2026-09-06) — ★★★★ **SIGN INTO A PRE-PLACED EMPTY `/FT /Sig` FIELD — `SignRequest::field_name` naming an existing empty merged signature field signs INTO it (its own `/Rect` + page place the appearance; `/V` set; `/SigFlags |= 3`; nothing appended to `/Annots` or `/Fields`); `/Lock` (Table 233) HONOURED as a `/FieldMDP` signature reference (§12.8.2.4, Table 256); `/SV` (Table 234) enforced in FULL — required-and-unmet refused by name with the satisfying values, recommended-and-unmet disclosed, unevaluable refused by name never skipped; six new `SignApplyError` variants; non-merged (`/Kids`) fields refused by name (narrowed)** — from *Backlog* (439th filing), never in *Next up*

**Before (`v0.41.0` + `10.12`):** `--field-name` only CREATED a field; a
name already in the AcroForm was refused as `FieldNameTaken`, so a document
with an author-placed "sign here" field could only be signed by adding a
SECOND field beside it; a `/Lock` on the author's field was never read and
no `/FieldMDP` was ever written; `/SV` was never read.

**After (`ab40127`):** the author's field is the target; its lock becomes
the `/FieldMDP` the author asked for; its seed values are checked before
anything is staged. Full account, criteria walk, tests, sweep and sourcing:
the 453rd head immediately above.

**What a caller sees, stated first.** `pdfcer sign --certify` with no level
prints `certification: DocMDP P=2 (form fill-in and signing) -- --mdp-level
not given; this is Table 254's default` (the choice is never silent; the whole
string is pinned by the CLI test);
`--mdp-level annotate` prints `P=3 (form fill-in, signing and annotations)`
and implies `--certify`; `pdfcer verify-signatures` on the output prints the
same `certification: DocMDP P=n (<meaning>)` line back. In core the request
is `SignRequest::certify: Option<MdpPermission>` — `MdpPermission::{NoChanges
(P=1), FormFillAndSign (P=2), FormFillSignAnnotate (P=3)}` with `p()`,
`from_p()` and `meaning()` so a shell prints words, never the bare integer;
`None` is the unchanged approval signature. `EditSession::sign` then writes,
in the SAME incremental update, `/Reference [<< /Type /SigRef
/TransformMethod /DocMDP /TransformParams << /Type /TransformParams /P n /V
/1.2 >> >>]` on the signature dictionary (`/V` a NAME, Table 254's note) and
`/Perms << /DocMDP <sig> >>` on the catalog (§12.8.4 Table 258 — the entry a
conforming reader SHALL enforce), merged into an existing `/Perms` and into
the catalog write the inline-AcroForm registration already produces — one
write per object per command. Table 253's `DigestMethod`/`DigestValue` are
OMITTED, cited: *"Optional; deprecated in PDF 2.0"* (ISO 32000-2 corrigendum
#117; spec-RAG row `SI-E8`). Two refusals BEFORE any allocation
(§12.8.2.2.1): `SignApplyError::AlreadyCertified { permission }` (one
certification per document) and `SignApplyError::CertificationNotFirst {
existing }` (the certifier is *"the person applying the first signature"*);
each names the remedy — sign without `--certify`. The 10.9 `P=1` refusal
(`CertificationForbids`) is now reachable from pdfcer's OWN certification.
Read side: `SignatureVerdict::certification: Option<u8>` (P, default 2 when
the params omit it — the SAME reading `signature::census` applies, so
verifier and census cannot disagree about one file);
`SignReport::certification: Option<MdpPermission>` echoes what was written.

**The seven draft criteria, walked (the 439th filing's list, in the *Backlog*
entry — kept in place, struck and annotated, because two were amended at ship
time):**

1. **`/Reference` SigRef + `/Perms /DocMDP` in the SAME incremental update;
   digest entries omitted with the clause cited — MET.** `DigestMethod`
   omitted, Table 253 *"Optional; deprecated in PDF 2.0"* — corrigendum #117
   cited in the rustdoc (`apply.rs:147`, `edit.rs:41513`); `SI-E8` is the
   spec-RAG row that sources it.
2. **`--mdp-level none|form-fill|annotate` → 1/2/3; `--certify` alone = 2,
   PRINTED as defaulted — MET.** `--mdp-level` implies `--certify`
   (`main.rs:27328`); the default sentence is pinned by
   `certify_without_a_level_takes_the_default_and_says_so`.

   both `SignApplyError` variants, both before staging (`edit.rs:41407–41415`);

defect (`Sabotage::{None, DigestUnderContextTag, UnsortedAttributes,
ReorderedAfterSigning, WrongMessageDigest}`, `cms_build.rs:139`);
`tests/sign_hardening.rs` splices it into a really-signed `hello.pdf` over
the file's REAL byte-range digest (asserting the byte ranges did not move)
and asks both. A `Sabotage::None` control proves the splice itself is
accepted, so the refusals are the defects' doing. A `.pfx` with NO
`localKeyId` pairs key and leaf by public-key identity
(`rsa2048-nolocalkeyid.pfx`). pdfcer signs on top of a pyHanko signature and
pyHanko countersigns pdfcer's output — BOTH directions measured. ECDSA P-384
end to end (`ecp384-modern.pfx`).

**Acceptance criteria walked (the 439th's six):** **1 MET, and 1(b) AMENDED
BY MEASUREMENT.** (a) attributes digested under the `0xA0` wire tag (`CB-4`)
→ both reject (`attributes_digested_under_the_context_tag_are_rejected_by_both`);
(c) a wrong `message-digest` → both reject
(`a_wrong_message_digest_is_rejected_by_both`). (b) expected *"`SET OF`
attributes emitted out of X.690 §11.6 order → both reject"* — MEASURED
2026-09-06: an unsorted set SIGNED CONSISTENTLY (the signature covers those
exact bytes) is ACCEPTED by both pdfcer and OpenSSL 1.1.1 — neither
re-encodes the set canonically before hashing; both hash the attributes AS
RECEIVED, retagged `0x31`
(`an_unsorted_set_signed_consistently_is_accepted_by_both_as_received`,
asserting `(true, true)` — the test pins AGREEMENT with the oracle, so a
divergence either way is noticed). pdfcer keeps the oracle's rule ON
PURPOSE: a stricter verifier would refuse signatures every other reader
accepts, and the tamper that IS an attack — attributes REORDERED AFTER
SIGNING — is caught by the as-received rule
(`Sabotage::ReorderedAfterSigning`,
`attributes_reordered_after_signing_are_rejected_by_both`, `(false, false)`);
a canonicalising verifier would ACCEPT that one, which is why as-received is
the safer rule, not merely the lenient one. So the criterion's three
sabotages became FOUR tests plus a control, and the one it mis-predicted is
recorded as a measurement, not rewritten. **2 MET:** `gen-signing-fixtures.py`
mints `rsa2048-nolocalkeyid.pfx` (2,613 B) from the SAME RSA material as
`rsa2048-modern.pfx` — cert bag exported in plaintext (`-certpbe NONE`),
every `localKeyId` bag attribute removed with asn1crypto, the SHA-256 MAC
recomputed by a Python port of the Appendix B.2 KDF (`strip_local_key_id`);
the test (`a_store_without_local_key_id_pairs_key_and_leaf_by_public_key`)
proves the OID is ABSENT from the store, the MAC verified, the paired leaf
`==` `rsa2048.cer`, and signs with it. The generator now ADDS shapes from the
existing material by default; `--regen` re-mints everything. **3 MET, BOTH
directions MEASURED** (pyHanko was available; neither half is "not
measured"): `tools/gen-foreign-signature-fixtures.py` (84 lines; pyHanko
generator-side only, rule 13) → `foreign-pyhanko-first.pdf` (7,144 B) and
`pdfcer-then-pyhanko.pdf` (32,599 B); pdfcer (ECDSA P-256) signs on top of
the pyHanko signature → both verify, the foreign `/ByteRange` intact, OpenSSL
verifies pdfcer's (`pdfcer_signs_on_top_of_a_pyhanko_signature_and_both_verify`);
the pyHanko countersignature (field `ForeignSig`) over pdfcer's output → both
verify (`a_pyhanko_countersignature_over_pdfcer_output_leaves_both_verifiable`).
pyHanko stamps the clock, so the bytes are not reproducible and the committed
file IS the fixture (`PROVENANCE.md`). **4 MET (relayed, with its
denominator):** `tools/content-identity` over 7 signed outputs (RSA / EC-256 /
EC-384 / no-lkid / visible / foreign ×2) — **7 files / 7 content streams / 7
byte-identical / 0 corrupted — GATE PASS**; and every signing test now
asserts `out[..base.len()] == base` (the incremental update touches nothing
below the old EOF). **5 MET on the pdfcer half; the Reader half NOT
MEASURED.** Frame + composed lines as above
(`the_appearance_carries_signer_date_reason_and_location`); overflow refused
before staging
(`a_rectangle_too_small_for_the_appearance_is_refused_before_any_write`).
Rendered with `render-page` and inspected — the box shows all four lines, the
frame intact (relayed). **Acrobat Reader was NOT driven**; the criterion's
*"Acrobat Reader displays it"* clause is recorded as NOT MEASURED, not as
passed. The GRAPHIC (logo / image) was never in scope. **6 MET:** the store
the criterion's IF waited on was ADDED — `ecp384-modern.pfx` (1,419 B) /
`ecp384.cer` / `ecp384.key.der` (secp384r1, PBES2 / AES-256-CBC, MAC
SHA-256) — and `EcdsaP384Sha384` runs end to end through pdfcer's verifier
and OpenSSL (`ecdsa_p384_signs_and_both_verifiers_accept_it`). The 20260903
RAG lesson's *"P-384 has no end-to-end fixture"* is amended in place this
filing (below).

**RAG (tier 5) — WRITTEN this filing:**
`C:\personal_rag\pdf\lesson_20260906_cms_signed_attributes_are_verified_as_received_not_resorted.md`
(quirk / HIGH) — CMS `signedAttrs` are verified AS RECEIVED, not re-sorted:
OpenSSL 1.1.1 `cms -verify` and pdfcer both accept a `SET OF` emitted out of
X.690 §11.6 order when the signature covers those exact bytes; a strict
re-encoding verifier would reject what Acrobat-class readers accept, and
would PASS the post-signing reorder that as-received catches. Builder: sort
BEFORE signing (DER) and never touch attribute order after. Verifier: hash
the received content under a `0x31` tag. Subject and master indexes updated;
the 20260903 lesson footnoted.

### `Pass 256.1` (`56dde4d`, 2026-09-05) — ★★ **`/ToUnicode` PARTIAL INVERSION — a composite font's character map is inverted PER CHARACTER, not per font: `ToUnicodeCMap::partial_inverse() -> Result<PartialInverse { unambiguous, ambiguous, multi_char_codes, empty_codes }, NotInjective>`; a character produced by exactly ONE code is written exactly, a character produced by SEVERAL is refused BY NAME at that character with every candidate code (`RInvTrigger::Ambiguous`, *"gives 'A' to 2 different codes (1, 2) … every other character of this font still edits"*), and only a map with NOTHING invertible (`TooLarge`/`Empty`) still refuses the whole font; the `EditReport` names the font's ambiguous characters (first eight) even when the replacement avoided them; `edit-text` with no new flag** — ★ **the 439th's census was NOT run; exposure stays unmeasured, and the narrowing shipped on cost**

**Before (`Pass 29.0`'s rule, measured in source at `8a18e53` by the 439th):**
a composite run was refused when `/ToUnicode` was absent OR non-injective —
`injective_inverse()` erred if ANY Unicode string was produced by two or
more CIDs, and `classify_font` turned that into `R-INV-4` for the WHOLE
font. The ABSENT half is untouched by this Pass (*"the information is not
in the file"* stays true, and is the third test).

**After.** `partial_inverse()` (`cmap.rs:750`) walks the singles and the
`bfrange`s once, keeping the same `MAX_BF_ENTRIES` ceiling
(`NotInjective::TooLarge`); every single-character destination is bucketed
by `char` — one producer → `unambiguous`, several → `ambiguous` with the
codes in ascending order; multi-character destinations (ligatures) and empty
destinations are counted (`multi_char_codes`, `empty_codes`), not inverted;
a map whose two maps are both empty is `NotInjective::Empty`.
`CompositeEncoding::build` (`encoding.rs`) consumes the result, so a font
with collisions BUILDS an encoder; `encode_str` checks `ambiguous` FIRST for
each character (`encoding.rs:300–325`) and refuses there with
`RInvTrigger::Ambiguous`, then `reverse` (the composite `R-INV-1`,
unchanged); `ambiguous_chars()` (`encoding.rs:288`) exposes the set.
`plan_edit_target` (`text_edit/edit.rs:1873–1899`) adds the success-path
disclosure. `classify_font` (`text_edit/edit.rs:3053`) swaps
`injective_inverse` for `partial_inverse` and widens its sentence to *"cannot
be inverted at all"*.

  worker `format.rs:3625`) — the requester's proposed name, kept. `find` /

### `Pass 256.0` (`1343f0e`, 2026-09-05) — ★★★★ **EDIT TEXT ACROSS SHOW OPERATORS — a `find` matches across CONSECUTIVE `Tj`/`TJ` operators of one text object when they share font resource name, size, `Tc`/`Tw`/`Tz`, marked-content sequence and text-space ROW, so a producer that writes ONE GLYPH PER SHOW OPERATOR (the operator's own document) and ordinary `TJ`-split kerning output are editable as one run; the replacement lands in the operator holding the match END, the earlier matched glyphs are removed, emptied operators stay as `() Tj`, and the line's `Td` followers RE-SPACE — `EditReport::operators_spanned`, `edit-text` with no new flag** — ★ **measured on the operator's file: `"clien"` → `"client"`, `operators_spanned=5`, `followers_repositioned=4`, advance `+8.032`**

**Origin.** The 439th filing's mint — the `pdfcer-gui` correction of
2026-09-05, ask (a): *"What a caret in a line of one-glyph-per-operator text
means is 'replace this span of the visual line', which is N operators."*
The operator's first real typo (`clien` → `client`, page 2 of `apartment
work - signed.pdf`) sat in a stream reading `(\x00\x17) Tj 16.076 0 Td
(\x00\x11) Tj 8.031 0 Td …` — one two-byte code, one `Td`, one `Tj`, per
letter. `edit-text` located `--find` inside ONE show operator by contract,
so a five-letter find was `NoMatch`: correct, and useless. The pin
(`Pass 145.0`) fixed the letter but left the tail un-respaced. Filed

**THE SPAN RULE — pdfcer's own, published on `find_anchor_span` /
`spannable` (`crates/pdfcer-core/src/text_edit/edit.rs:2567` / `:2542`).**
Acrobat's grouping is unpublished (`Acrobat_Features\text_edit__in_place_editing_mechanism.md`,
recorded GAP; its `must_have` is that pdfcer document its own). A `find` may
match across CONSECUTIVE show operators (`Tj`/`TJ`) of ONE text object when
they share: the font RESOURCE NAME (not `/BaseFont` — two resources with one
name are two fonts here), the size, character and word spacing (`Tc`/`Tw`),
horizontal scale (`Tz`), the marked-content sequence (`MCID`), and the same
text-space ROW — every text-matrix component but the x translation. The
records BETWEEN them may only be x-only `Td`s, same-row `Tm`s, or ignorable
operators. **A pinned request never spans** (the pin names one operator; that
is its meaning). `find_anchor` (single operator, `:2649`) is tried FIRST, so
every edit that matched before matches the same way and reports
`operators_spanned = 1`.

**What the edit does (`plan_edit_target`, `:1696`).**
- The replacement is re-encoded through the run's OWN font — the `R-INV`
  ladder and the embedded-subset floor are UNCHANGED — and written into the
  operator holding the match END; the matched glyphs are removed from the
  earlier operators.
- **Emptied-operator disposition, DECIDED (criterion 2 left it to the
  engineer): kept as an empty `() Tj`.** The producer's own positioning
  chain — its `Td` per glyph — stays intact and is re-spaced by the follower
  logic rather than folded away. Disclosed in the `span:` report line and
  the module docs.
- `match_range` (`:2868`) generalises `match_run` (`:2837`) to a character
  range that may cross `TJ` ELEMENTS: `MatchRun` gains `elem_hi` and
  `kern_advance` (the kern numbers swallowed between the first and last
  matched element, carried as an advance so the delta is exact), and
  `emit_edited_operator` (`:3166`) collapses `elem..=elem_hi` into one
  string. Inside one operator `edit_text` uses `match_range` too, so
  `[(cli) -20 (en)] TJ` edits with `operators_spanned = 1` and the kern
  consumed. **`match_run` keeps refusing cross-element for `format_text`,
  whose emitter has not learnt it — `format_text` is still single-operator
  (not in scope, by name in the mint).**
- **FOLLOWERS (`reposition_followers`, `:2259`) — WIDENED past criterion 3.**
  `Td`/`TD` are now recorded as `Rec::Td { tx, ty, leading }` (`:855`)
  instead of an opaque `Boundary`. The walk from the first edited operator
  carries `cum` (total advance change so far) and `absorbed` (what the
  positioning chain has already realised): an x-only `Td` is shifted by
  `cum − absorbed` — it is RELATIVE, so the shift propagates by the
  operator's own semantics; an absolute `Tm` on the row by `cum`; a `Td`
  with `ty ≠ 0` (a NEW LINE) is rewritten `tx − absorbed` so the next line
  lands exactly where the producer put it, and the walk stops. **Exception,
  disclosed:** when a later line in the same text object uses `T*`, `'` or
  `"` (no operands to compensate), `Td` steps are NOT rewritten — the
  pre-256.0 behaviour — and a `relayout:` disclosure (`:2343`) says the text
  after the edit keeps the producer's positions and may crowd or gap.
  Rewritten `Td` operands are ROUNDED to 1/10 000 pt so f32 glyph widths do
  not smear `28.80000114`-shaped noise across the line; the absolute-`Tm`
  path is unchanged.
- `EditReport::operators_spanned: u64` (`:594`) — `1` for every
  pre-256.0-shaped edit, so the field is never absent; the CLI prints
  `operators_spanned=` on its summary line (`main.rs:22817`) and a `span:`
  disclosure line names the count and the `() Tj` disposition
  (`edit.rs:1972`). `check-outcome-disclosed` clean.
- `format.rs` (`+4/−4`): the two `Rec::Boundary` breaks also break on
  `Rec::Td`, so `format_text` and synthetic-italic behaviour are
  byte-identical to before.

### `Pass 14.5` (`8670523`, 2026-09-05) — **`EditableTextModel::hit_test` COULD NOT ANSWER `None` ON ANY PAGE THAT CARRIED TEXT — its fallback took the nearest line at ANY distance, so a click on blank paper always found a caret; a line is now IN REACH only within ONE LINE-HEIGHT of its box, and beyond that the answer is `None`** — ★★ **the doc comment described the defect as a contract:** *"Returns `None` only when the page has no clustered glyph at all"* — ★ **measured by the requester at 100 000 pt and at 1e9 pt: `None` returned ZERO times in ~30 probes on two documents**

**The defect.** `hit_test(x, y)` (`crates/pdfcer-core/src/text_edit/model.rs`,
shipped 2026-08-01 in `Pass 14.0` as the caret-placement query behind every
on-canvas text click) picked a line in three steps: a box CONTAINING the
point wins; else the vertically-nearest line whose box spans `y`; else —
the fallback — the nearest line by baseline distance **with no threshold at
all** (`best_dy` started at `f64::MAX` and nothing compared it to a bound).
So `chosen` was `Some` whenever `self.lines` was non-empty, and
`hit_in_line`'s clamp then snapped the caret to that line's nearest end.
**`None` was structurally unreachable on any page with a single line of
text.** The doc comment said exactly that — *"Returns `None` only when the
page has no clustered glyph at all"* — and the requester read it, correctly,
as a description rather than a defect; it had stood since `Pass 14.0`. The
`Pass 14.3` UI spec (`docs/ui_specs/pass-14.3-text-edit-ui.md:296–297`) had
specified the OTHER contract from the start — *"`None` (page has no
clustered glyph at all, **or the click missed every line**)"* — and the
implementation never delivered the second clause until now.

**The measurement (requester's, re-derived before filing rather than
quoted — their own words: two requests that week had been filed on
diagnoses that did not survive re-measurement).** A standalone binary
against `pdfcer-core` at pin `b1033ab` (`v0.39.0`; the function byte-identical
at `afc199d`) probed `hit_test` at a ladder of offsets from a run's own
`bbox`:

| document | probe | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `apartment work - signed.pdf` p.2, run 0 (`bbox=[33.47 736.22 288.90 757.90]`, `MediaBox` `[0 7.9 612 799.9]`) | right +0 / +215 / +1 000 / **+100 000 pt** (at `x` = 100 288.9) | run 0, offset 25 — all four |
| same | below −200 / −1 000 / −100 000 pt | run 12, then run 31, run 31 (walks to the last line and stays) |
| same | 10 k above-right of the page; 10 k below-left; **(1e9, 1e9)** | run 0; run 31; run 0 |
| `D:\Dev\pdfTests\SW41177\SW41177.pdf` p.1 (1584 × 1224, 457 runs, 164 lines) | right +100 000 pt; below −100 000 pt; (1e9, 1e9) | run 0 `" 55"`; run 284 `"1"`; run 314 `"1"` |

**Across both documents and thirty-odd probes, `None` was returned 0 times
(0 of ~30).** The +100 000 pt case is the tell: `y` sat inside the line's
box, so the SECOND step's `contains_y` arm chose the line without ever
testing `x`. An earlier note in that shell had recorded 215 pt right and
99 pt below as the failure distances; the re-measurement showed there was
no distance at which the answer changed.

**What it cost the requester.** Their one-text-tool gesture (operator,
2026-08-19: *"How do I make new text when I click on the canvas and expect
to edit there?"*) turns `hit_test` → `None` into a new-text origin at the
click (`place.rs:129`, trace `text-edit-became-add
reason=no-run-under-the-click`). **That arm has never fired on a real
document.** The only surviving route to their `NoRun` was an empty run's
text (`place.rs:446`) — a different condition. `edit.add_text` never asks
the hit test, so nothing was impossible; the two doors were meant to be one
and nothing on screen said which the operator stood at. They declined to
work around it (decision 058 shape): a shell-side distance check could not
tell a deliberate 3 pt snap from an unbounded fallback (both are
`Some(TextPosition)`), and any threshold would be a second opinion about
this crate's geometry (`direction`, `hit_in_line`'s clamp) — the `R221`
drift shape.

**The fix (their shape (a), chosen for their stated reason).** A line is
**in reach** when the point lies inside its box inflated by one line-height
on every side, `reach = max(line.size, bbox height, 0)`. A containing box
still wins outright; otherwise the nearest-by-baseline line **among those in
reach**; otherwise `None`. `hit_in_line` is byte-unchanged, so the gestures
every editor relies on survive — click just past the last character → caret
after it; click a little above or below a line → that line. The bound is
derived from the line rather than passed as a parameter, so **every
caller, including ones not yet written, gets presence semantics with no
second opinion about the geometry** — shape (b) `hit_test_within(x, y,
max)` and shape (c) `Hit { position, snapped }` were both declined for
that reason. For a rotated line the bound is its page-space box inflated
the same way: generous, never tighter than the line. `+69/−21` in ONE
file: the body, the doc comment (which now records the change and the
measurement in place of the old sentence), and one unit test.

**Tests.** New `hit_test_answers_none_beyond_one_line_height_of_every_line`
— a 10 pt `"Hi"` at (72, 700), box ≈ x 72..82 × y 700..710, reach 10 pt:

below) and **5 `None` assertions** (215 pt right; 200 pt below; 30 pt above;
(1e9, 1e9); (−1e4, −1e4) off the sheet) — 9 of 9 green. Every EXISTING
hit-test consumer unchanged and green: `tests/rotated_text.rs` (723 lines,
the `Pass 139.x` sweeps), `tests/text_edit.rs` (181 lines), and the model's
own tests. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `check-string-gaps`
green (engineer's shell, relayed).

**★★★ 440th filing, 2026-09-05 (late) — NO PASS SHIPPED. DECISION 138
AUTHORED: CI CAUGHT A FEATURE WIDENING ON THE BATCH PUSH, AND THE RELEASE IS
HELD FOR IT.** CI run `33994927156` on `8a18e53` (the 439th's 7-commit

declared `features = ["oid"]` (its `Cargo.toml:174–178` — an IMPLICIT
optional-dep feature; no `sha2` key exists in its `[features]` table), and
Cargo feature unification puts `oid` on pdfcer-core's own
`default-features = false` `sha2` line. `oid` = `digest/oid` = `const-oid`
`AssociatedOid` impls for the SHA-2 types, nothing else — no backend change,
no new `unsafe`, `const-oid 0.10.2` already in the tree (`cargo tree -i
const-oid --depth 1`: `der`, `digest`, `rsa`). Load-bearing:
`rsa::pkcs1v15::SigningKey::<D>::new` requires `D: Digest + AssociatedOid`
for the RFC 8017 §9.2 `DigestInfo` prefix — the `RsaPkcs1Sha256` arm of
`Pass 10.7` does not compile without it. **Ruling (decision 138):** 039's
`sha2` acceptance extends to `oid`; `alloc` and `zeroize` stay forbidden
(zeroize: `FileKey` sits in a plain `Vec<u8>` — zeroizing the hash state
would be theatre). Guard regex `(alloc|oid|zeroize)` → `(alloc|zeroize)`,
comment and error message name 138: `1c6f670` *"ci: decision 138 — allow
sha2 `oid` (rsa/sha2 feature edge) in the decision-039 guard"*, `+16/−10`,
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` only. Also filed: `796ff8c` (engineer memory,

**Acceptance criteria, as filed at the 436th filing → as built.**

1. **The `Signer` trait — MET IN INTENT, DEVIATED IN SHAPE, and the deviation
   is the one design fact a `Pass 10.10` implementer must read.** Filed:
   *"`sign(digest) -> signature` takes the ALREADY-COMPUTED digest, never the
   message"*. Shipped: `fn sign(&self, algorithm: SignatureAlgorithm, message:
   &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SignError>` (`mod.rs:223`) — the trait takes the
   **MESSAGE** (the `0x31`-retagged signedAttrs DER) and the signer hashes it
   under `algorithm`. **Why:** `rsa 0.10.0-rc.18`'s `pkcs1v15::SigningKey` has
   **no `RandomizedPrehashSigner` impl**, so BLINDED prehash signing — the
   only RSA path decision 137 permits — is unreachable; blinding exists only
   through `RandomizedDigestSigner`, which consumes the message (SESSION_LOG
   438th entry, gotcha 2). A digest-in trait would have forced either an
   unblinded RSA path (forbidden) or a second pipeline. **Consequence for
   `Pass 10.10`:** a custodial signer (CNG `NCryptSignHash`, PKCS#11 `C_Sign`)
   hashes the message itself under the named algorithm and hands the
   custodian the digest — one extra hash on the shell side, still one
   pipeline. **The design note is MET:** `SignatureAlgorithm` {`RsaPkcs1Sha256`,
   `RsaPssSha256`, `EcdsaP256Sha256`, `EcdsaP384Sha384`} is an explicit
   parameter carrying its DER `AlgorithmIdentifier` (PSS params hand-encoded
   per RFC 4055) and digest OID, so `Pass 10.8` wraps the bytes correctly by
   construction. `certificate_chain()` returns DER leaf-first — met. Two
   members the criterion did not ask for: `default_algorithm()` (RSA v1.5 for
   an RSA key, ECDSA for an EC key) and `key_label()`. `pub fn
   verify_raw_signature(cert, alg, msg, sig)` (`mod.rs:454`) is the in-crate
   oracle any shell `Signer` can test against.
2. **PFX v3, password-integrity mode** — met. Public-key-integrity mode

3. **MAC first as the password check** — met; wrong password →

4. **Accept BER inside the PFX (`P12-14`) — DEVIATED: REFUSED BY NAME, NOT

7. **Key ↔ leaf by `localKeyId`, fallback public-key identity; chain leaf →

### `Pass 10.8` (`7734261`, 2026-09-05) — **BUILD THE CMS `SignedData` — CAdES for PAdES B-B: `version 1`, detached `id-data`, signedAttrs {content-type, message-digest, `signing-certificate-v2`}, NO signing-time, the `0x31` retag by construction over an X.690 §11.6-sorted `SET OF`, one signer, the full chain, no `crls`; an IN-HOUSE DER writer (decision 137), accepted by pdfcer's verifier AND by OpenSSL**

definite lengths, minimal INTEGER, OIDs, `set_of` sorted by full encoding),
`sign/cms_build.rs` (210). Oracle plumbing in `tests/sign_document.rs`

**Acceptance criteria → as built.**

1. **`SignedData.version = 1`, `digestAlgorithms = { id-sha256 }`,
   `certificates` = the full chain, `crls` OMITTED** — met.
2. **Detached: `eContent` absent** — met.
3. **`SignerInfo` v1, `sid = issuerAndSerialNumber`** — met.
4. **Exactly three signed attributes, DER-sorted** — met: `content-type` =
   `id-data`; `message-digest` = the `/ByteRange` SHA-256 as an OCTET STRING
   inside the `SET OF AttributeValue`; `signing-certificate-v2` (RFC 5035)
   with `certHash` = SHA-256 over the whole DER leaf, `hashAlgorithm`
   **OMITTED because it is the ASN.1 DEFAULT** (`CB-7` — the ASN.1 followed,
   the SHA-1 prose ignored), `issuerSerial` WRITTEN. **No `signing-time`**
   (`PC-3`) — the same attribute set for `adbe.pkcs7.detached`; `/M` carries
   the claim in both. `signing-certificate` v1 never authored.
5. **The `0x31` retag** — met **by construction**: one `set_of` encoding is
   produced, that encoding (tag `0x31`) is what is signed, and the same bytes
   are re-tagged `[0] IMPLICIT` (`0xA0`) on the wire — there is no second
   serialisation to drift. The `SET OF` sort is X.690 §11.6, ascending by full
   encoding, and `der_out.rs`'s unit test
   `set_of_sorts_by_encoding_not_by_insertion` proves the writer sorts.
6. **Algorithms** — met: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-256 DEFAULT for an RSA key;
   RSASSA-PSS SHA-256 as an option with RFC 4055 params (SHA-256, MGF1
   SHA-256, salt 32) hand-encoded in `signatureAlgorithm`; ECDSA
   `ecdsa-with-SHA256` / `-SHA384`, the OCTET STRING wrapping DER
   `SEQUENCE { r, s }`. SHA-1 and MD5 never authored; SHA-384/512 for RSA not
   offered (the criterion made them optional).
7. **DER throughout, definite lengths only; exactly one `SignerInfo`** — met.
   `unsignedAttrs` absent (B-B).
8. **Oracle, both directions — met for RSA v1.5, RSA-PSS and ECDSA P-256:**

### `Pass 10.9` (`7734261`, 2026-09-05) — **THE PDF-LEVEL SIGNING WRITE — `EditSession::sign(signer, &SignRequest, &SaveOptions) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, SignReport), SignApplyError>` + `pdfcer sign`: a merged `/FT /Sig` widget, `/AcroForm /SigFlags 3`, the Table 252 dictionary with `/SubFilter /ETSI.CAdES.detached` BY DEFAULT and `/M` REQUIRED, fixed-width `/ByteRange` sentinels + a zero-filled `/Contents` hole, ALWAYS an incremental update, `/ByteRange` to EOF, back-patched by same-length overwrites only, SELF-VERIFIED before returning; the Pass 0 stub's `[not yet implemented]` is GONE. APPROVAL signatures only — certifying (`--certify --mdp`) NOT built, a recorded deviation**

`SignRequest`, `SignReport`, `CommandKind::AddSignatureField`),
`sign/apply.rs` (508: hole geometry, back-patch, self-verify),
`crates/pdfcer-cli/src/main.rs` (+368: the `sign` subcommand replacing the
stub), `crates/pdfcer-cli/Cargo.toml` (new `signing` feature, default ON,

(verb count **202 → 203**, `check-core-api-verbs` PASS), `README.md`.

**Acceptance criteria → as built.**

1. **Signature field + widget** — met with one stated first-cut limit and one
   deviation. Merged field/widget `/FT /Sig`, `/T` unique, `/V` → the
   signature dictionary, `/Subtype /Widget`, `/P`; **invisible default
   `/Rect [0 0 0 0]`, `/F 132`** (Print + Locked), no `/AP`. Visible
   (`--visible x0,y0,x1,y1 --page P`): the caller's rect, `/F 4`, and a
   **thin-frame `/AP` — TEXT IS NOT DRAWN** (the criterion asked for
   *"plain text: subject + `/M`"*); the CLI doc says so: *"the details
   (signer, time) live in the signature panel of any reader, not in the
   frame — a composed appearance is a later increment."* A stated first-cut
   limit, not silence. **DEVIATION: signing INTO an existing empty
   `/FT /Sig` field by name is NOT built** — `--field-name` names the NEW
   field, and a collision is refused (`SignApplyError::FieldNameTaken`), not
   filled. Owed when a pre-placed-field workflow needs it.
2. **`/AcroForm` created if absent, widget in `/Fields`, `/SigFlags 3`, page
   `/Annots` gains the widget** — met.
3. **The signature dictionary** — met: `/Type /Sig`, `/Filter /Adobe.PPKLite`,
   `/SubFilter /ETSI.CAdES.detached` DEFAULT, `adbe.pkcs7.detached` via
   `--format pkcs7`; **`/M` REQUIRED and written verbatim** — a non-PDF-date
   → `SignApplyError::SigningTimeNotPdfDate`; `/Name` `/Reason` `/Location`
   `/ContactInfo` optional pass-throughs; **NO `/Cert`**; `/ByteRange`
   exactly four integers. **The CLI derives UTC now from the system clock
   when `--signing-time` is absent (Hinnant `civil_from_days`, no
   dependency) AND PRINTS that it did** — the report's `time_derived` field
   and the stdout sentence *"was DERIVED from this machine's clock"*. The
   criterion spelt the key `m_source=system-clock`; the fact is the same,
   the spelling differs — met in substance.
4. **The two-pass hole** — met: ten-digit `/ByteRange` sentinels
   (`1000000000`) back-patched with zero-padded integers; a zero-filled
   `/Contents` of `reserve` bytes — **default 12 288 (12 KiB), not the
   criterion's "~16 KB"**; the hole located in the appended revision with
   the `<`/`>` delimiters inside the gap; `/ByteRange [0 a b len−b]` reaching
   EOF; SHA-256 over span 1 ‖ span 2; `2N ≤ L` else
   `ReservationTooSmall { needed, reserved }` — **never shrunk**; back-patch
   is same-length overwrites only. The test asserts the BASE file is a
   byte-identical prefix of the output (nothing before the appended revision
   changes); a before/after comparison of the tail outside `(a, b)` is not a
   separate assertion.
5. **ALWAYS incremental** — met by construction: `to_incremental_bytes` is
   the only path; a full rewrite is **not offered** rather than *"refused by
   name"* — the `&SaveOptions` parameter cannot select one. A recovered
   base → `SignApplyError::RecoveredBase` (R67's refusal, surfaced). A staged
   deferred redaction → `RedactionPending`.
6. **`/Contents` never encrypted / never wrapped** — MOOT in this cut:
   encrypted documents are refused outright (7a), so no encrypting path
   reaches the signature dictionary yet. Owed alongside 7a.
7. **Refusals by name — three DEVIATIONS recorded:**
   - **(a) Encrypted document — REFUSED OUTRIGHT (`SignApplyError::Encrypted`),
     NOT permission-bit-gated as filed.** Reason: `save_incremental` cannot
     append to an encrypted base yet — `Pass 5.4`'s criterion-7 branch choice
     (incremental-save-on-encrypted refused by name) — and the error text
     says exactly that (*"the incremental writer cannot append to one
     yet"*). The filed two-permission gate (fill-in-forms for an existing
     field; + modify for a new one) is owed when the writer learns encrypted
     bases; refusing on `/Encrypt` today is the honest boundary of the
     writer, not a claim that encrypted PDFs cannot be signed.
   - **(b) Certified document — refuses `/DocMDP /P 1` ONLY**
     (`CertificationForbids { permission: 1 }`); `/P 2` and `/P 3` permit a
     further APPROVAL signature per Table 254 — this is the filed reading
     (*"`/P 2` and `/P 3` permit a further APPROVAL signature only"*), met.
     The 436th head's shorthand *"past its MDP"* is this.
   - **(c) A second CERTIFYING signature — NOT A CASE YET**, because pdfcer
     authors no certifying signature at all in this cut (see 8). Recorded so
     the refusal is added when certification is.
   - Hole too small (4), recovered base (5) — met.
8. **Certifying vs approval — DEVIATION: NOT BUILT.** `--certify --mdp 1|2|3`,
   the `/Reference [<< /TransformMethod /DocMDP … >>]` array and the catalog
   `/Perms /DocMDP` are absent; **every signature this cut writes is an
   APPROVAL signature.** Owed as its own increment (an operator may want a
   `Pass 10.12`); the read side (`SignatureImpact`, `Pass 3.2`) already
   classifies what such a signature would mean.
9. **Self-verify before returning** — met: the output bytes are re-parsed and
   `signature_verify` must return `Integrity::Verified` with
   `covers_to_eof`; anything else → `SelfVerificationFailed` and nothing is
   written. `PlaceholderNotFound { what }` names a hole the writer could not
   find.
10. **A second signature on an already-signed document** — met on pdfcer's
    OWN output: `a_second_signature_appends_and_the_first_still_verifies`
    (EC over the RSA-signed `hello.pdf`) — the new field is `Signature2`,
    both verify, the first covers only its own revision. **The pyHanko-signed
    `Pass 10.1` fixture half of the criterion is NOT tested.**
11. **CLI — the stub is FILLED, not duplicated.** `sign <in> --cert <pfx>
    [--password <pw>] -o <out> [--format cades|pkcs7]
    [--algorithm rsa-pkcs1|rsa-pss|ecdsa-p256|ecdsa-p384] [--signing-time D:…]
    [--name --reason --location --contact] [--field-name F]
    [--visible x0,y0,x1,y1 --page P] [--reserve N]`. **Not shipped from the
    filed surface: `--certify --mdp` (8), `--dry-run`, and a password PROMPT
    — `--password` is a command-line argument with an empty default**
    (`main.rs:1871`–`1873`); the criterion's *"prompt, never echoed, never an
    env-var default"* is met only in its last clause. Stdout: the PKCS#12
    report (MAC algorithm / iterations, key scheme, chain) then one `sign`
    line carrying `field`, `subtype`, `algorithm`, `key`, `signer`, `serial`,
    `certificates`, `byte_range`, `cms_bytes`, `reserved`, `signing_time`,
    `time_derived`, **`level=B-B`** (the level ACTUALLY produced — `PC-12`),
    `prior_signatures`, `self_verified`, `out_bytes`. Exit **12** on
    refusal / self-verify failure, **9** on a refused request, **3** I/O.
    Behind the CLI's new `signing` feature (default ON). **Driven live by
    the engineer:** `sign` `hello.pdf` → `verify-signatures` 1/1 verified;
    second `sign` (EC, `--format pkcs7 --visible 100,100,300,160 --page 1
    --name Ken`) → 2/2; wrong password → exit 12 with the MAC error; legacy
    `.pfx` + `--algorithm rsa-pss` ok.
12. **Rule 4** — met: the only inference is the clock-derived `/M`, and it is
    printed. The GUI half is `pdfcer-gui`'s.

**Design note filed in `docs/core-api/02` §1.31 (engineer's, relayed):** the
returned `Vec<u8>` IS the signed document; the `EditSession` is NOT advanced
onto it — `CommandKind::AddSignatureField` stays in the old session's history
and the caller re-opens the returned bytes for any further edit. A shell that
keeps editing the old session and saves it would write an unsigned document.
